# Vendored marks

Third-party logos, kept here as files and not linked from their own
sites: the console makes no request a reader did not cause, and an
asset named by a content hash on somebody else's deploy is a 404
waiting to happen.

| File | What it is | Where it came from | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `hex.svg` | the Hex logo (hex.pm) | `https://hex.pm/images/hex-full-a8183c4f9adac71516516d107d402b18.svg`, fetched 2026-09-23 | the house's `.pkg-ref` (assets/design/build.py): every mention of an Elixir package, wherever the console names one |
| `github.svg` | the GitHub Invertocat, black | `GitHub_Invertocat_Black.svg` in `https://brand.github.com/GitHub_Logos.zip` (linked from `https://github.com/logos`), fetched 2026-09-28 | the `.pkg-ref` of a package that comes from a repository on GitHub, on the light ground |
| `github-white.svg` | the GitHub Invertocat, white | `GitHub_Invertocat_White.svg`, same pack | the same mention on the dark ground: GitHub draws the mark in black on light and white on dark, so the console carries both and shows the one the ground calls for, rather than recolouring one |

Each is used to identify the site it links to, and for nothing else —
it says where the link goes, and the workbench claims no association
with it. The marks stay as their owners drew them: no recolouring, no
redrawing.
